sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Barron County, WI?
sections.html:
The county Register of Deeds records deeds for Barron County property. That office keeps the county's real estate records along with its vital records, and it is listed among the departments on the county website.

Its job is to protect the official repository of real estate records and keep it open to the public. One point matters to sellers: the office offers no real estate searches. Order any title search through your title company or closing agent, and use the register only to record.

Under s. 59.43, the register records each document offered that the law allows, stamps it with the date, hour and minute, and takes documents in the order they arrive.

Most documents cost $30 to record in Barron County, a flat fee set by state law in s. 59.43(2)(ag). Whoever asks for the service pays in advance.

The rest of the state schedule is short:

  • $30 for a deed, mortgage, satisfaction or other document entitled to be recorded.
  • $50 for a cemetery plat, subdivision plat or condominium plat.
  • $2 for the first page of a copy and $1 for each added page.
  • $1 more to certify a copy.

Recorded real estate documents come back only if you supply a self-addressed stamped envelope for a paper copy or an email address for a PDF, so put one or the other in the packet. A recording and filing fee schedule is posted by the Wisconsin Register of Deeds Association.

sections.h2: How much is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a Barron County sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays 30 cents for each $100 of value, which works out to $3 per $1,000, on any taxable deed (s. 77.22). The county's median owner-occupied home value is $216,600.

Value means the full price paid or to be paid, liens included. On a land contract it is the total principal the buyer agrees to pay. The register collects the fee when the deed is submitted, and seller and buyer both sign the return. The register has no duty to check your value or your exemption claim, so accuracy rests with the people who sign. The county keeps 20 percent of the fee and the rest goes to the state (s. 77.24).

The Department of Revenue now takes the Real Estate Transfer Return through My Tax Account. Have these items ready before you start:

  • The completed deed.
  • Name, address, phone and email for each seller and buyer.
  • A Social Security number, ITIN or FEIN for each party.
  • The parcel numbers from the property tax bill.

After you submit, print the receipt and bring it with the notarized deed and payment. Some counties accept this packet electronically, so ask the Barron County office which way it prefers. A transfer that spans two counties needs a separate return for each. If the department finds the value understated by 25 percent or more, or an exemption claimed wrongly, the penalty is $25 or 25 percent of the added fee, whichever is greater. Questions go to RETR@wisconsin.gov or 608-264-6885.

sections.h2: Which Barron County transfers owe no transfer fee?
sections.html:
A deed owes no fee only when it fits an exemption in s. 77.25, and the deed itself must name the subsection that applies. The usual ones for home transfers:

  • Transfers by will, descent or survivorship.
  • Gifts or nominal-price transfers between parent and child, stepparent and stepchild, or grandparent and grandchild.
  • Transfers between spouses.
  • A foreclosure, or a deed in lieu of foreclosure, to the mortgage holder.
  • Real estate worth $1,000 or less.
  • A deed that corrects or confirms an earlier recorded conveyance for nominal or no consideration.

Exemptions are read narrowly. If the return does not offer the exemption you expected, the transfer is subject to the fee. When a house passes within a family, check this list before paying a fee you may not owe.

sections.h2: How must a deed be formatted for Barron County to accept it?
sections.html:
A deed has to meet the standard document format in s. 59.43(2m), or the register may refuse it. The main rules:

  • Leave the upper right corner of page one blank, at least 3 by 3 inches, for the recording stamp.
  • Put the document title within the top 6 inches and return information on page one.
  • List the parcel identification number for every parcel the document affects.
  • Use white paper of at least 20 pound weight, 8.5 inches wide and 11 or 14 inches long, with pages not hinged.
  • Print in black, blue or red ink, with a top margin of half an inch and other margins of a quarter inch.
  • Show the name of whoever drafted the document, and type or print the grantor, grantee and notary names clearly.

Original signatures must be notarized or authenticated, and the transfer return and fee or exemption number must travel with the deed. A Social Security number on a document is a separate problem, because under s. 59.43(1m) a register may not record a document that contains one. If a group of related documents is marked as one transaction and any one fails, the register may return the whole group unrecorded.

sections.h2: Can you record electronically in Barron County?
sections.html:
Yes. The county maintains a list of trusted e-recording submitters with five vendors on it: CSC eRecording, EPN (Erecording Partners Network), Indecomm Global Service, Simplifile (a division of ICE Mortgage Technology) and Hopdox.

Ask your closing agent whether the file will go through one of these channels or arrive on paper, and confirm the Barron County register will take it that way before signing day.

Barron County is mostly rural, with four cities: Barron (the county seat), Chetek, Cumberland and Rice Lake. Population has been flat and the share of older residents is high.

sections.h2: What should a seller have ready before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Gather the paperwork before closing day so recording does not hold up the sale. Most of this list comes straight from the sections above:

  • The signed, notarized deed with the full legal description. The shortened description on a tax bill is not acceptable.
  • The parcel number from the Barron County tax bill.
  • The Real Estate Transfer Return receipt, or the exemption subsection if no fee applies.
  • Payment of the $30 recording fee and any transfer fee.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope or an email address for the return copy.

Ask the closing agent to confirm each item the day before closing.

A cash buyer skips the lender's underwriting and appraisal, which often shortens the timeline. Recording works the same way, though. The deed still has to meet the format rules, the transfer return still has to be filed, and the fee or exemption still has to be settled. If the deed is ready early, a cash closing can be recorded quickly, so check the format list and the return receipt a few days before the date you set.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Barron County?
faqs.a: $30 under s. 59.43(2)(ag), Wisconsin Statutes. Subdivision, condominium and cemetery plats cost $50. The seller also owes the state transfer fee of $3 per $1,000 of value unless an exemption applies.

faqs.q: Who pays the Wisconsin real estate transfer fee?
faqs.a: The seller, who is the grantor on the deed. Section 77.22 puts the fee on the grantor at 30 cents per $100 of value. Both seller and buyer sign the transfer return, and the register collects the fee when the deed is submitted.

faqs.q: Does the Barron County Register of Deeds search titles for me?
faqs.a: No. The office offers no real estate searches. Ask your title company or closing agent to run the search, then bring the finished deed to the register to record.

faqs.q: Can a deed with a Social Security number be recorded?
faqs.a: No. Under s. 59.43(1m), a register of deeds may not record a document that contains an individual's Social Security number. Keep the number off the deed, since the transfer return collects party identifiers separately through the Department of Revenue system.

faqs.q: How do I get my recorded deed back from Barron County?
faqs.a: Include a self-addressed stamped envelope for a paper copy or an email address for a PDF. Recorded real estate documents come back only with one of these. Copies ordered later cost $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page.
